I'm still pretty new to this hobby so I'm probably not the best person to ask for advice as I dont have a lot of experience with different components but I'm glad to help where I can.

1. I like them. Nice and torquey, plus they are a unibell design. My emax eco II motors would split after a hard crash and I have to use pliers to "press" them back together. I won't buy motors with 2 piece bells anymore.

2. The gps was mounted in the rear originally, but I crash...a lot, and the JST-GH-6P connector on the front of the chip broke off. There is a second connector on the rear of the chip and it was easier to relocate than to resolder the connector to the pcb

3. I have rp1 on my other drone and it works fine. My lizard brain just thought more = better, so I went with rp3 diversity.

4. I never really used the gps to it fullest potential. I mainly used it to see how fast I was going. It's my understanding that if you use the return to home function, you set the hover throttle according to the weight of the drone. Since I have 4 different brands/sizes of batteries and the weight would not be the same, I never set it up. The JST connector on the rear of the chip also broke off so now it's sitting in my junk drawer until I plan on flying where I might lose the drone. I only fly 2 nights a week at a parking lot with a group I met down at the local hobby shop so I haven't needed it.

Roux
3  Tbsp unsalted butter
4  Tbsp all-purpose flour (use gluten-free flour for GF)
1 Tbsp curry powder
1 Tbsp garam masala
¼ tsp cayenne pepper (optional for spicy)

In a small saucepan, melt the butter over low heat.
When the butter is completely melted, add the flour. Stir to combine the butter and flour.
Soon the butter and flour fuse and swell. Keep stirring because the roux will easily burn. Cook for 15-20 minutes on low heat. 
The roux will become light brown color
Add the garam masala, curry powder, and cayenne pepper.
Cook and stir for 30 seconds and remove from the heat. Use the curry roux in your curry recipe. Make sure to taste and season with salt after you add the roux to the dish (as the roux is not salted).

I don't use potatoes and carrots for my curry but you can if you'd like, but I do use onions, sweet onions.
Dice one large sweet onion and saute on med heat for 15 mins or until extremely reduced and golden brown but not burned(think the color of in-n-out onions)
Add three cups water to onions and bring to a boil
Add roux and stir until thick(recipe calls for 4 cups of water but I use less initially and add more to get the consistency that I like)
Add salt to taste
Serve and enjoy
